name: coding
label: Coding

tools.name: rg
tools.use: Search the code. The first move on any codebase question: find the definition, the callers, the string.
tools.args: A pattern and a path, relative to the workspace. -n prints line numbers, -i ignores case, -l lists files only.

tools.name: git
tools.use: Version control: status, diff, log, blame, branch, commit. Commit only when asked.
tools.args: Ordinary git arguments. The workspace is the repository root when the project has one.

tools.name: node
tools.use: Run JavaScript — a project script, a test runner already vendored in node_modules, or -e for a quick check.
tools.args: A script path, or -e and a program.

tools.name: npm
tools.use: Install dependencies and run package scripts: npm install, npm test, npm run build. This box has network access, so a registry is reachable.
tools.args: A script invocation or an install. Prefer `ci` over `install` when a lockfile is present, so the tree matches it exactly.

tools.name: python3
tools.use: Run Python — a script from the workspace, or -c for a quick check. Standard library only.
tools.args: A script path, or -c and a program.

tools.name: jq
tools.use: Filter or reshape JSON — a package.json field, a config value, tool output.
tools.args: A jq filter, then a file — or nothing after it to read stdin.

notes: This box has network access, so dependency installs work — prefer `npm ci` or a lockfile-respecting install so the tree matches what the project pins. Run the project's tests before and after a change. Use the file tools for edits: they act on the same files a command sees under /workspace. Reaching the network is the one thing here that leaves the machine, so treat what you send as visible.
